title: Reuse architecture knowledge, device snapshots and measurements at different scopes
applies_when: Onboarding a new GPU or reusing hardware knowledge across devices, hosts, drivers or operator workloads.
lesson: Reuse official architecture semantics by architecture and document revision; query actual SKU/partition capacities and host topology separately. Keep empirical rates bound to probe, precision, shape, layout, cache regime, runtime and power/clock/load conditions. Reuse the method on another device, then run a cheap canary before transferring numerical rates. Preserve unavailable fields and known query limitations so the next agent does not repeat unsupported probes without a relevant environment change.
avoid_when: Matching architecture or marketing names does not prove equal SM counts, bandwidth, partition size or connectivity. A live inventory or empty process list is not an allocation/idleness guarantee; check load and memory too, especially with container visibility restrictions. Negotiated link metadata is not payload bandwidth, and an empirical reference is not a physical ceiling.

evidence.note: Documents device identity, query availability, link and runtime-dependent management observations. Supports cheap per-device revalidation, not transfer of private benchmark rates.
Documents timing and effective-bandwidth interpretation, memory hierarchy and performance dependencies. Supports scoped measurement reuse; no per-device performance number is asserted here.
